allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 13 m at 25 years and 24 m at 50. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: bright green fronds, pale grey trunk, and the crownshaft's shining green sheaths, drawn as sixteen upright cards round the trunk's top (Sargent 1922: bright green cylinders of densely imbricated sheaths).

generator.params.note: Sargent (1922, Roystonea regia, pp. 107-108): leaves 10 to 12 ft (3 to 3.7 m) long, frond_length 3.5 m; pinnae 2.5 to 3 ft (0.76 to 0.9 m) long, leaflet_length 0.24 of the frond; the green upper part of the stem, the crownshaft of leaf-stalk sheaths, 8 to 10 ft (2.4 to 3 m), drawn as a 2 m shaft plus the trunk the living fronds stand on; a trunk 80 to 100 ft tall and often 2 ft (0.6 m) through, rising from an abruptly enlarged base (flare 0.6) and enlarged near the middle, tapering to both ends (a belly 0.35 wider at 22 years, so trunk_radius 0.22 m is 0.3 m at its widest); a broad head of gracefully drooping leaves (hang 25 degrees over a frond's life). Closely pinnate: 45 pieces of rachis, so about 90 leaflets a side, linear-lanceolate cards 1.5 inches wide on 2.5 to 3 ft (aspect 0.045). Set by eye: twelve fronds a year living a year and a half, about eighteen in the crown, and leaflets standing 18 degrees above and below their V for the plumed look.

generator.params.fan_arch.note: What the palm program's values mean for a palm's stated characters: its frond is its whole leaf; fan or feather from its division pattern, with the petiole, its girth, rachis pieces and frond angles of the built-in fan or feather palms; suckers if it is clonal; the trunk's rise from its usual height less the crown, and its girth from its stated diameter or else its height.

generator.params.suckers.note: What the palm program's values mean for a palm's stated characters: its frond is its whole leaf; fan or feather from its division pattern, with the petiole, its girth, rachis pieces and frond angles of the built-in fan or feather palms; suckers if it is clonal; the trunk's rise from its usual height less the crown, and its girth from its stated diameter or else its height.

generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the palm base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the palm program gave as defaults until then.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy (plant forms milestone F4). Calibration against measurements and photographs comes later.
